title: Don't Build Agents, Build Skills Instead – Barry Zhang & Mahesh Murag, Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic argues that general agents should be built around a thin runtime with filesystem/code access, MCP connectivity, and a library of skills: versionable folders of procedural knowledge and scripts. Skills are progressively disclosed, can be created by agents, and should be treated like software with testing, versioning, dependencies, and sharing across an organization.

takeaways.technique: Versioned skill folders for recurring procedures
takeaways.what_they_do: They package procedural knowledge as folders containing skill.md, scripts, assets, and instructions, versionable in Git and shareable like files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Skills are organized collections of files that package composable procedural knowledge for agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: Only skill metadata is shown at runtime; the agent reads the full skill.md and supporting files only when it decides the skill is relevant.
takeaways.evidence_quote: At runtime, only this metadata is shown to the model just to indicate that he has the skill.

takeaways.technique: Save repeated code as deterministic skill scripts
takeaways.what_they_do: When the model repeatedly writes the same script, they save it inside the skill as a reusable tool for future runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We kept seeing Claude write the same Python script over and over again

takeaways.technique: Test skill triggering and output quality
takeaways.what_they_do: They propose treating skills like software, with testing/evaluation for whether agents load the right skill at the right time and whether output quality matches expectations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: exploring testing and evaluation, better tooling to make sure that these agents are loading and triggering skills at the right time

takeaways.what_they_do: Skills give agents a standardized place to write down reusable procedures so future versions of the same agent can use them efficiently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Anything that cloud writes down can be used efficiently by a future version of itself.

takeaways.what_they_do: They describe skills as a collective knowledge base so that when one agent or team member learns something, other agents in the org benefit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of the agents inside your team and your org get better as well.
